subject: forensic-medicine
title: Xanthoproteic Reaction, Carbolic Acid and Carboluria

steps.title: Xanthoproteic reaction names nitric acid
steps.tx: The **xanthoproteic reaction** is the yellow staining of skin, tissue and protein by nitric acid, which nitrates aromatic amino acids into yellow picric acid type compounds. Yellow coronets on the teeth, yellow skin and yellow clothing stains therefore name nitric acid rather than sulphuric acid, which chars brown black. The reaction is a scene test in words: colour of stain plus corrosion pattern separates the mineral acids before any laboratory report arrives.
steps.say: Yellow stain on skin, teeth and cloth is nitric acid signing its work, while sulphuric acid chars brown and black.

steps.title: Carbolic acid, phenol crystals
steps.tx: **Carbolic acid or phenol** forms short colourless prismatic needle crystals with a burning sweetish taste and the familiar carbolic smell, turning pink and liquefying in air; commercial acid is a dark brown liquid rich in cresol. Lysol is a fifty percent cresol solution in saponified oil, and phenol is about eight times as toxic as lysol. Dettol is a chlorinated phenol with terpineol. Ten to fifteen grams kill in three to four hours.
steps.say: Needle crystals smelling of carbolic, eight times lysol's strength, kill at ten to fifteen grams within hours.

right.title: Related preparations
points: Lysol, fifty percent cresol in oil

steps.title: Phenol anaesthetises what it burns
steps.tx: Phenol precipitates protein, coagulates cell contents and destroys nerve endings, so **carbolic skin burns** begin as a hard cracked whitish opaque eschar that is strikingly painless from local anaesthesia, then falls away leaving a brown stain. Deep burns are black, necrotic tissue turns green white or brown white and sloughs readily, and lysol stains tissues brownish purple. The painless white eschar is the bedside clue that separates phenol from mineral acid burns, which hurt intensely.
steps.say: A white painless eschar that later stains brown is phenol burning with built in anaesthesia, unlike screaming acid burns.

steps.tx: Phenol precipitates protein, coagulates cells, and destroys nerve endings, so **carbolic skin burns** open as a hard, cracked, whitish opaque eschar that is strikingly painless. The plaque later falls away and leaves a brown stain. Deep burns are black. Necrotic tissue may look green white or brown white and sloughs easily, and lysol colours tissue brownish purple. The painless white eschar separates phenol from mineral acids, which cause immediate severe pain.
steps.say: Phenol makes a hard white eschar that does not hurt because nerve endings are destroyed, then the area stains brown. Deep tissue may turn black or green white. Mineral acid burns, by contrast, are intensely painful from the start.

steps.title: Systemic carbolism
steps.tx: Absorbed phenol is a nervous system depressant, especially of the respiratory centre, under **acute carbolism**. Headache, giddiness and coma develop with subnormal temperature, contracted pupils, stertorous breathing, rapid feeble irregular pulse, cold sweat and dusky cyanosis, with phenol odour on the breath. Haemolysis and methaemoglobinaemia are characteristic. Death comes by syncope, respiratory failure, glottis oedema or aspiration bronchopneumonia. Vapour inhalation can produce the whole systemic picture without gut corrosion.
steps.say: Cold sweat, contracted pupils, stertor and phenol breath mark carbolism, and inhaled vapour alone can produce it.

steps.title: Carboluria, urine that darkens in air
steps.tx: **Carboluria** is the urine of phenol poisoning: scanty at first with albumin and free haemoglobin, colourless or slightly green when passed, then turning green or even black on exposure to air. Phenol is oxidised in the body to hydroquinone and pyrocatechol, excreted free and conjugated, and their further oxidation in standing urine makes the colour. A urine sample darkening in the specimen jar is therefore diagnostic evidence worth photographing and preserving.
steps.say: Urine that leaves the body pale and blackens in the jar is carboluria, phenol metabolites oxidising in open air.

steps.tx: **Carboluria** is the urine of phenol poisoning. It is scanty at first and contains albumin and free haemoglobin. Freshly passed, it is colourless or slightly green, then turns green or even black in air. Phenol is oxidised in the body to hydroquinone and pyrocatechol, excreted free and conjugated, and those products oxidise further in the standing jar. A sample that darkens on the bench should be photographed and kept as evidence.
steps.say: Phenol urine is scanty, may contain albumin and haemoglobin, and leaves the body pale or faintly green. Hydroquinone and pyrocatechol then darken it to green or black in the open jar.

vis.alt: A urine specimen jar darkens from green toward black as it stands in air.
vis.caption: Freshly passed urine looks pale or faintly green, then turns dark green and black in the open jar. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Carbolic acid is the lavage exception
steps.tx: Among corrosives, **carbolic acid alone permits gastric lavage** with care, the standing exception to the no lavage rule for corrosive poisoning. The reason is mechanistic: phenol hardens and anaesthetises the mucosa rather than charring it into friable tissue, and its greater danger is rapid systemic absorption, which lavage reduces. Olive oil, castor oil, magnesium or sodium sulphate, demulcents and ten percent alcohol or glycerine washing of skin complete the standard management Reddy describes.
steps.say: Phenol is the one corrosive you may lavage, because stopping its absorption matters more than the hardened wall risks.

nodes.label: Identify phenol by eschar and smell
Wash skin with alcohol or glycerine

steps.title: Chronic phenol poisoning, phenol marasmus
steps.tx: **Chronic carbolic acid poisoning or phenol marasmus** brings anorexia, weight loss, headache, vertigo, dark urine and pigmentation of skin and sclera. Hydroquinone and pyrocatechol deposit in cornea and cartilages producing ochronosis, the same pigmentation classically linked to alkaptonuria where homogentisic acid darkens cartilages, ligaments and fibrous tissue. Occupational exposure in disinfectant workers is the usual source, and removal from exposure is the first treatment.
steps.say: Wasting, dark urine and cartilage pigmentation in a disinfectant worker is phenol marasmus until exposure is removed.

steps.title: Xanthoproteic and other colour tests at the scene
steps.tx: Colour reactions give rapid orientation in **acid identification by staining**: nitric acid yellows, sulphuric acid chars black, carbolic acid whitens then browns, oxalic acid bleaches mucosa white, and copper sulphate, met next lesson, stains vomit and stomach green blue. Barium solution precipitates white barium sulphate from sulphuric acid and white barium oxalate, soluble in hydrochloric acid, from oxalic acid. Scene colours narrow the laboratory request but never replace chemical analysis of preserved samples.
steps.say: Yellow, black, white brown, bleached or green blue: stain colours triage the acids while the laboratory confirms them.

steps.title: Circumstances of phenol poisoning
steps.tx: Phenol's disinfectant ubiquity shapes its cases under **circumstances of carbolic poisoning**: accidental ingestion from unlabelled bottles and skin absorption during disinfection work, suicidal drinking of household disinfectant, and abortifacient misuse by vaginal application. Because phenol absorbs through intact skin, serous cavities, rectum and vagina, splashes over large areas can kill without a drop being swallowed. The phenolic smell on breath and clothing often reaches the examiner before the history does.
steps.say: Unlabelled disinfectant bottles, skin absorption at work and suicidal drinking make most phenol cases, announced by their smell.
